2.  **Approximate Intersection Test:** Perform an intersection test between the view frustum (or camera ray) and the bounding box; unlike conservative culling, this test may return visible even if the primitive is occluded, justifying false-negatives to reduce duplicated fragments [S2].

The claim states that the approximate intersection test performs a test between the view frustum/camera ray and the bounding box, and that it may return visible even if the primitive is occluded (false-negatives) to reduce duplicated fragments. The evidence in Source [S2] explicitly mentions 'Approximate Tile-Wise Culling' which justifies 'intersection test with false-negatives' to reduce 'duplicated fragments' and 'rendering times'. The evidence confirms the purpose (reducing duplicated fragments) and the nature of the test (approximate intersection test with false-negatives). While the specific geometric detail 'view frustum (or camera ray)' vs 'tile-wise' is a slight variation in terminology (tile-wise implies a projection of the frustum/camera rays onto tiles), the core assertion that the test allows false-negatives to reduce duplicated fragments is fully supported by the text.
